title: Ground stop briefly issued at O'Hare Airport ‘due to staffing' at start of busy holiday week
excerpt: A ground stop has been issued at Chicago's O'Hare Airport at the start of the busy Thanksgiving holiday travel week, the FAA announced Monday.
content_html:
According to the FAA, "departures to Chicago O'Hare International are grounded due to staffing" until at least 12:15 p.m.

By Alex Dvorak • Published November 23, 2026 • Updated on November 23, 2026 at 3:56 pm

A ground stop was briefly issued at Chicago's O'Hare International Airport Monday by the Federal Aviation Administration.

According to the FAA, "departures to Chicago O'Hare International are grounded due to staffing," but those restrictions have since been lifted.

"The FAA is briefly pausing flights into Chicago O'Hare International Airport due to staffing constraints at Chicago Terminal Radar Approach Control (TRACON)," the FAA said in a statement to NBC Chicago.

Further details on what caused the staffing problem weren't immediately clear.

By 12:30 p.m., the ground stop had been removed from the FAA's website, though some departure delays remained.

The Chicago Department of Aviation had previously warned travelers of heavy traffic on roadways around the airport due to large crowds expected for Thanksgiving week.

Check back for more on this developing story.
